title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Selenium (Se, Z=34) is 78.971(8)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Selenium (Se, Z=34) as 78.971(8), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 34, symbol Se, as Selenium. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Selenium as 78.971(8). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. Range in isotopic composition of normal terrestrial material prevents a more precise standard atomic weight being given; the tabulated atomic-weight value and uncertainty should be applicable to normal materials. Isotope rows in the same file: Se-74 relative atomic mass 73.922475934(15), isotopic composition 0.0089(4); Se-76 relative atomic mass 75.919213704(17), isotopic composition 0.0937(29); Se-77 relative atomic mass 76.919914154(67), isotopic composition 0.0763(16); Se-78 relative atomic mass 77.91730928(20), isotopic composition 0.2377(28); Se-80 relative atomic mass 79.9165218(13), isotopic composition 0.4961(41); Se-82 relative atomic mass 81.9166995(15), isotopic composition 0.0873(22). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
